title: Repo and Reverse Repo Agreements

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This page describes the New York Fed's Open Market Trading Desk authority to conduct repo and reverse repo transactions as directed by the FOMC to implement monetary policy and maintain the fed funds rate within the target range. Repos temporarily increase reserve balances (economically similar to collateralized loans) while reverse repos temporarily reduce them (economically similar to collateralized borrowings). The Desk conducts overnight reverse repo (ON RRP) and standing repo (SRP) operations each business day at FOMC-set rates, serving as floor and ceiling mechanisms for money market rates respectively.
key_points: The Desk is authorized by the FOMC to conduct repo and reverse repo operations to maintain the fed funds rate within the target range
Repo transactions: Desk purchases securities from counterparties with agreement to resell, temporarily increasing reserve supply (economically similar to collateralized loans)
Reverse repo transactions: Desk sells securities to counterparties with agreement to repurchase, temporarily reducing reserve supply (economically similar to collateralized borrowings)

ON RRP operations provide a floor under overnight interest rates by offering a risk-free investment to institutions ineligible to earn IORB; eligible collateral is U.S. Treasury securities from SOMA portfolio
SRP operations provide a ceiling on money market rates by limiting upward pressure; eligible collateral includes Treasury, agency debt, and agency MBS
ON RRP counterparties include primary dealers, banks, money market mutual funds, and GSEs; SRP counterparties are primary dealers and eligible depository institutions
The Desk can conduct unscheduled operations as needed to maintain the fed funds rate within target range
Recent announcements referenced: April 3, 2026 statement on operations; March 12, 2026 statement on repo small value exercise
why_it_matters: This page explains the foundational market plumbing mechanisms the Federal Reserve uses to control short-term interest rates. ON RRP and SRP operations create the corridor system (floor and ceiling) within which the fed funds rate operates. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for comprehending how monetary policy is transmitted to money markets and ultimately to broader financial conditions.
market_structure_context: ON RRP and SRP form the technical framework for Fed policy implementation. ON RRP provides a floor by absorbing excess reserves when rates fall below IORB. SRP provides a ceiling by lending reserves when markets face upward rate pressure. Both operations use pre-announced rates set by the FOMC and are conducted daily by the Trading Desk. The page references transaction data published quarterly approximately two years after conduct per Dodd-Frank Act requirements.
